planting.note: Plant nursery-propagated rhizomes in fall in deep, humus-rich, evenly moist but well-drained soil in a cool, sheltered, shaded woodland or shaded rock-garden setting.

directions: Set nursery-propagated rhizomes at a shallow depth in fall into rich, slightly acid to neutral humus with reliable moisture and dappled to full shade, then mulch annually with leaf mold to mimic the cool forest litter of its native Himalayan range. This diminutive relative of the familiar North American trilliums bears a single small, upright maroon-purple flower with narrow, erect petals above a whorl of diamond-shaped mottled leaves, opening in mid-spring before the tree canopy fills in. It is extremely slow to reach flowering size from seed or division and should never be sourced from wild-collected stock, since unsustainable harvest of the rhizomes for traditional medicine has pushed wild populations toward endangered status across its Afghanistan-to-Bhutan range. Give it a permanently cool, humid root run - a raised shaded bed or trough is ideal in warmer gardens - and avoid summer drought or waterlogging alike.
